ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Jim Bridger

code.originalText: Fifteen-week review five weeks after left cataract surgery: vision with new glasses, driving, back pain and knees

text.paragraph: Fifteen-week review five weeks after left cataract surgery. [S]

Mr. Bridger returns five weeks after phacoemulsification of the left cataract. The surgeon's checks at one day and one week were normal, and he had his one-month check with refraction at the eye clinic this morning; his new glasses are ordered. He finished the left steroid drops a week ago. He says both eyes now see as they did when he was young, and the glare at night has gone. He has had no falls since the spring. He finished formal physical therapy last week and does his exercises at home most mornings; his back pain averages about 3 out of 10. His wrist is fully better. His knees ache on the orchard slopes but less with the gel. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-07-21; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Crepitus and bony enlargement; no effusion; full extension

Gradual, painless blurring of vision in both eyes over about two years, worse in the right, with glare from sunlight and oncoming headlights, faded colors, and trouble recognizing faces across a room; Snellen acuity 20/200 right and 20/100 left with his old glasses, no better with a pinhole; no flashes, floaters, pain or redness; cause under evaluation with an ophthalmology consultation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented failing eyesight; superseded when the consultation found bilateral cataract.

Bilateral age-related nuclear cataract, dense and brunescent in the right eye and moderate in the left, with cortical spokes; the cause of his reduced vision, glare and color loss; no glaucoma, macular degeneration or diabetic retinopathy; treated with sequential cataract surgery
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, linked to his documented loss of sight; not a retrospective diagnosis of his real blindness, whose cause is not recorded.

Chronic low back pain for many years, aching across the lower back and worst on the side of an old arrow-wound scar over the right lower back, stiff in the morning and after long rides in his truck; no leg pain, numbness, weakness, bladder or bowel change, fever or weight loss; no red flags
S — Synthetic chronic back pain anchored to his documented arrow wound; which side of the back the arrowhead lay in is not recorded, and the right side is a synthetic choice.
Nontoxic multinodular goiter, present for decades: a firm, nodular, non-tender thyroid enlargement with no pressure symptoms (no trouble swallowing or breathing, no voice change); euthyroid
S — Synthetic modern classification of his documented goiter; the type of his real goiter is not recorded.
Primary osteoarthritis of both knees, aching on stairs and after walking the orchard, with morning stiffness under half an hour, crepitus and bony enlargement
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented rheumatism; the old term does not name a modern diagnosis.
One fall in the past year, missing the bottom step of the porch at dusk, without injury; poor vision in low light and contrast; at risk of further falls
S — Synthetic fall linked to the reduced vision.
Sprain of the right wrist from a fall on the porch steps three weeks after the first cataract operation, when the two eyes saw differently; X-ray without fracture; healed
S — Synthetic acute injury at the sick visit; not a historical claim.
Lens implants in both eyes after sequential phacoemulsification cataract surgery, right then left six weeks apart; best-corrected vision about 20/20 in each eye with new glasses
S — Synthetic status after the modern cataract surgery.
